questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Promotion: Identification of Business Opportunity' refers to.
questions.a: Promotion is the first stage of company formation in which the promoter conceives the business idea, investigates its feasibility, assembles resources and takes steps to set up the company, and the promoter stands in a fiduciary position towards the company.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Promotion: Identification of Business Opportunity'.
questions.a: The promoter performs discovery of the idea, detailed investigation, financing, assembling the business unit and entering into preliminary contracts before incorporation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Promotion: Identification of Business Opportunity' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Incorporation: Registration Documents and Certificate' refers to.
questions.a: Incorporation brings the company into legal existence through registration with the Registrar of Companies by filing the memorandum of association, articles of association, declaration and the prescribed fee, after which a certificate of incorporation is issued granting the company its birth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Incorporation: Registration Documents and Certificate'.
questions.a: From the date of the certificate of incorporation, the company becomes an artificial person with separate legal entity and perpetual succession.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Incorporation: Registration Documents and Certificate' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Capital Subscription: SEBI and Minimum Subscription

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Capital Subscription: SEBI and Minimum Subscription' refers to.
questions.a: After incorporation the company raises capital through public subscription, requiring a name approval earlier, securities from SEBI, filing of prospectus or statement in lieu of prospectus, minimum subscription, and allotment of shares after the application money is received.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Capital Subscription: SEBI and Minimum Subscription'.
questions.a: Minimum subscription is the minimum amount stated in the prospectus that must be raised before allotment, and SEBI regulates the disclosure and investor protection norms of public issues.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Capital Subscription: SEBI and Minimum Subscription' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Capital subscription (source: kebs107.txt capital subscription stage section)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Commencement of Business' refers to.
questions.a: A public company must obtain a certificate of commencement of business by filing the statement of share capital and a declaration that minimum subscription has been raised before it can start operations or borrow, while a private company can begin business after incorporation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Commencement of Business'.
questions.a: The certificate of commencement of business is the final licence that lets a public company start its operations.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Commencement of Business' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Commencement of business (source: kebs107.txt commencement stage section)
